seo.title: Oracle Database client for {devices}
seo.description: Connect to Oracle Database without Instant Client, run SQL and PL/SQL scripts, read DBMS_OUTPUT, and start Data Pump exports on the server.

header.title: Oracle Database client
header.lead: Run SQL and PL/SQL without installing Oracle Instant Client. Read DBMS_OUTPUT alongside query results.

sections.title: Connect
paragraphs: Enter a host, listener port and Service Name, or choose SID in <ui>Connection Type</ui>. Password sign-in supports Normal, SYSDBA and SYSOPER roles.

Native Network Encryption needs no setup: when the server asks for it, AES with a SHA-2 checksum is offered, and the <ui>Network Encryption</ui> setting changes what TablePro offers. For TLS, choose Required for TCPS, or Verify CA or Verify Identity with a CA certificate. New connections start with SSL off, and Preferred stays on plain TCP.

On Oracle Autonomous Database, copy the host, port and service name from the TLS connection string, not the mTLS one, and set SSL to Required or Verify CA. Wallet files are never read, so the database has to accept TLS without mutual TLS.
A RAC SCAN listener, a shared server or a load balancer in front of the database needs no configuration, and an <network>SSH tunnel</network> reaches a listener on a private network.

sections.title: SQL, PL/SQL and transactions
paragraphs: Run PL/SQL blocks and stored units as single statements. A / line ends a unit in scripts. Compilation errors include Oracle’s messages and source positions. SQL*Plus client commands are not supported.
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE lines show with the result of the statement that printed them, with no SET SERVEROUTPUT ON needed. In an anonymous block, :name is a query parameter you fill in from a panel.
Each statement commits when it succeeds. Start with SET TRANSACTION, SAVEPOINT or LOCK TABLE to hold changes, and everything after it waits for your COMMIT or ROLLBACK, grid saves included.

Each user is a schema, and ⌘K switches the active one without reconnecting. Row edits are staged with Preview SQL. A block that drops or truncates, even through EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, raises the dangerous query warning before it runs.

sections.title: Schema
paragraphs: Add, rename, modify and drop columns or create indexes in the <structure>Structure tab</structure>. Names are quoted when case-sensitive. Inspect primary keys, foreign keys and CREATE TABLE DDL.
A partitioned table lists its partitions under it, each with its position, and subpartitions nest under their partition. Query one with SELECT * FROM orders PARTITION (p2024).
Compare & Sync ({compareSyncTier}) compares Oracle schemas or data. Scripts use / separators for SQL*Plus or SQLcl.

sections.title: Export on the server
paragraphs: Server-Side Export starts a Data Pump job that writes a table to a DIRECTORY object on the server, under your own privileges. Nothing lands on your Mac. The job keeps running after the sheet reports it started; follow it in DBA_DATAPUMP_JOBS.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: Import {importFormats} files; when a data file creates a new table, its proposed name is upper case and fits Oracle’s length limit. Export tables or results as {exportFormats}. A SQL export follows each routine and trigger with a / line, so SQL*Plus can restore it.

sections.title: iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: On iPhone and iPad, the Oracle driver is part of the app. The connection form takes a Service Name or SID, the SYSDBA and SYSOPER roles and the Network Encryption setting. You browse tables as cards, edit rows that have a primary key and run SQL in the Query tab; creating or altering tables stays on the Mac.

faq.question: Why do I see none of my application’s tables?
faq.answer: You probably connected to the container database. A pluggable database has its own service name, such as XEPDB1 inside XE. Run lsnrctl services on the server to list the names the listener answers for.

faq.question: Why does SET SERVEROUTPUT ON fail?
faq.answer: SQL*Plus commands such as SET SERVEROUTPUT ON, SHOW ERRORS and EXEC are not SQL, so the server refuses them. Delete them: output is on from the moment you connect. Write EXEC p as BEGIN p; END;.

faq.question: Will an account with an old 10G password verifier connect?
faq.answer: Yes, though Oracle has deprecated the DES-based hashing it uses. Change the password with ALTER USER … IDENTIFIED BY and check that password_versions in dba_users then holds 11G or 12C.
